implementation_notes: C has neither a pool abstraction nor a resilience framework, so the bulkhead is hand-written: one sem_t per dependency provides the capacity bound (sem_init with the limit, sem_trywait or sem_timedwait for fail-fast or bounded waits, sem_post in every exit path), or one dedicated pthread set plus a bounded ring buffer per dependency provides worker isolation. Use the semaphore form when the caller should keep its own thread and only admission must be bounded; use the worker form when calls block and must not occupy the caller's pool. The classic structure is the only option here, so it is always justified; the real decision is which failure domain to partition (per dependency, per tenant, per worker group).
idiom_name: POSIX sem_t permit (or pthread worker pool) per dependency
pitfalls: A forgotten sem_post on an error path permanently leaks a permit and silently shrinks the bulkhead.
sem_trywait and sem_timedwait return -1 with EAGAIN or ETIMEDOUT; treating that as an I/O error instead of a saturation signal breaks the rejection policy.
Unnamed semaphores are not portable to every platform (macOS lacks them), so named semaphores or a pthread-mutex counter are the fallback.
A shared blocking worker pool provides no isolation at all: isolation exists only when each dependency gets its own threads or its own permit bound.
